atAGlance: Bánh mì ốp la is a breakfast bánh mì with sunny eggs, herbs, cucumber, pickles, chili, and Maggi-style soy seasoning, often cooked on a small street griddle.
whatItIs: Bánh mì ốp la is a fried-egg bánh mì, often served with runny eggs, pâté or soy seasoning, cucumber, pickles, cilantro, and chili. It is a beloved breakfast order.
howToEnjoy: Eat it early in the day when the eggs are hot and the bread is just warmed. If you like runny yolk, stay close to the stall and eat before it soaks too far into the loaf.
howLocalsOrder: Order bánh mì ốp la for breakfast-style comfort. Ask for no chili or egg well-done before the egg and bread are finished.
worthKnowing: Ốp la shows how Vietnamese breakfast can be quick but still vivid: French-influenced bread, local herbs, pickles, seasoning, and a hot egg all in one hand-held meal for people heading to school or work.
goodToKnow: Ask for không cay if you want the egg sandwich without chili.
